title: Promise Me the Spotlight Anime Unveils Teaser, Main Cast, Staff
content:
Bandai Namco Filmworks revealed on Wednesday the teaser trailer, key visual, main cast, and main staff members for the television anime of Jun Wakatsuki 's Promise Me the Spotlight ( Watashi o Center ni Suru to Chikaimasuka? ) manga. The company also revealed that the anime will air on TV Tokyo and its six affiliate channels.

The anime will star:

Haruna Mikawa as Mizuki "Zukki" Natsuno, the least popular but a hardworking member of the famous idol group Melty Strawberry, who is known for her stern expression and being curt

Taihi Kimura as Kōichi Okuta, a high school student and Mizuki's die-hard fan

Mai Kanno as Awayuki "A-chan" Shiroi, Melty Strawberry's undisputed center who captures the hearts of fans with her "cunningly cute" gestures

Yukari Anzai as Hatsune "Ha-chan" Fukuba, a polite and courteous member of Melty Strawberry who always looks after her fellow members

Bandai Namco Filmworks also revealed the character visuals for other members of Melty Strawberry:

Saku "Saku-chan" Kageyama, not a morning person and often blurts surprising things when groggy from sleep. She uses polite language when speaking to other members.

Niko 'Nikorin" Okamoto, a member with a signature bun hairstyle, supposedly inspired by takoyaki

Mio "Shiomin" Shiomi, the group's caring big sister figure

Mirin "Mii-chama" Satō, refers to herself as "boku" and prioritizes time efficiency

Minori "Minorin" Mochizuki, also refers to herself as "boku" and has a straightforward personality

Lala "Lala-pyon" Hoshino, the youngest and tallest member with a straightforward and energetic personality

Seiji Kishi ( Assassination Classroom two seasons, Yuki Yuna Is a Hero , Blue Orchestra ) is directing the anime at Team TillDawn . Yūko Kakihara ( Aikatsu Stars! , Blue Orchestra , Firefly Wedding ) is in charge of series scripts, and Kazuaki Morita ( Assassination Classroom two seasons, Blue Orchestra , Classroom of the Elite three seasons) is designing the characters.

Yuika performs the anime's opening theme song "Nanimono demo nakatta Watashi dakara" (Because I Was No One).

Kodansha 's K MANGA service publishes the manga and describes the series:

"If you can really make me the Center...then we can get married." Meet Mizuki Natsuno, the least popular member of the nationally acclaimed idol group, Melty Strawberry. She has an eternal fan in Koichi Okuta, who is always pouring heart and soul into supporting her. Normally, a fan would never get to interact with their idol beyond the stage. But one thing led to another, and Koichi now finds himself living together with Mizuki in his own house. He vows to make her the new Center of Melty Strawberry, sparking an unconventional tag-team between a devoted fan and his idol. Together, they attempt to elevate Mizuki's career from obscurity to stardom!

Wakatsuki launched the manga in Kodansha 's Shonen Magazine Edge magazine in 2022. The manga moved to Kodansha 's Magazine Pocket app when Shonen Magazine Edge ended publication in 2023. Kodansha published the manga's sixth compiled book volume on July 9.

title: Pero Pero★Sparkles Anime Reveals Cast, Staff, January Debut
content:
The official website for the television anime of Yurie Sekiya 's Pero Pero★Sparkles characters revealed the cast, staff, January premiere on TV Tokyo , and a new key visual for the anime on Wednesday.

The cast includes:

• Yuki Sakakihara as Mero

• Mai Kanno as Kyun

• Ai Fairouz as Ru

• Yōhei Azakami as Narrator

Mao Miyashita is directing the anime at Usagiou , and Yūji Umoto is in charge of the series scripts. Shiomi Yano is designing the characters, while Yui Ōzaki is the art director. Saya Fukase is directing the sound, and Shōta Kowashi is composing the music with TV Tokyo Music producing the music.

Sekiya launched the characters in 2013, and the characters have since spawned merchandise, as well as a 2020 YouTube anime.

title: Kemono Jihen Manga's Climax Is 'Imminent'
content:
The December issue of Shueisha 's Jump SQ. magazine confirmed on Wednesday that the story climax of Shō Aimoto 's Kemono Jihen manga is "imminent."

The 25th compiled book volume, which shipped on August 4, announced that the series will end in the next volume.

Seven Seas Entertainment publishes the manga in English and describes the story:

Inugami is a Tokyo detective who specializes in the occult. One day, answering a call to a remote village leads him to Dorotabo: a peculiar boy nicknamed after a yokai that haunts muddy rice paddies. The boy has no parents and is somewhat unnerving, emitting a foul odor that draws the ire of those around him. Inugami, however, quickly realizes that there's something more monstrous about Dorotabo than just his nickname–a fact proven when the two of them investigate an inhuman creature attacking local livestock. Perhaps Inugami can take this mistreated boy under his wing and train him to face the secret, supernatural beasts hidden in the world...using the eerie powers of his own body.

Aimoto launched the manga in Jump SQ. in December 2016. Seven Seas released the 22nd volume in English on October 6. The manga inspired a television anime that premiered in January 2021.

The series took a one-issue break in September following the death of Aimoto's brother in August.

The series took a one-issue break in February. Aimoto shared that she had gastroenteritis at the beginning of the year. Aimoto added that she is feeling better now and will also get an endoscopy soon.

title: Black Clover Creator Returns With Special Art After Finale
content:
Black Clover might have ended the manga’s 11 year run earlier this year, but series creator Yuki Tabata has returned with some special new art after that grand finale. Black Clover Season 2 has been taking over screens as each new episode have finally started to adapt the Spade Kingdom Raid arc that fans have been waiting five long years to see in action. It’s been a great time to be a fan of the franchise as a result with all sorts of fun new things coming out.

This includes a digital art book for Black Clover that’s begun to release in Japan . Though the final physical releases for Black Clover’ s manga have since come and gone, this new art book delivers cooler looks at some of the series’ best layouts and covers that fans can’t get anywhere else. That includes a new piece from Tabata released specifically for the new digital art book itself, and it gives one final look at everyone. Check it out below as spotted by @nite_baronX on X .

Black Clover Creator Releases New Art After Manga’s Finale

This final piece of Black Clover art from Tabata (at least for now) unfortunately doesn’t dig too deep on the series, but gives us a fun final look for each of the characters to go out on. There are some major moves, however, such as the tease of Yami and Charlotte on a date. Given that this was one of the few romances that the series actually decided to pull the trigger on at the end of the series’ run, it’s fun to see a nod to it here. But then again, it’s just fun to see everyone enjoying their happy ending one last time.

Black Clover ended its manga after 11 years of serialization earlier this Spring , and with it brought the end to the final arc that actually began a few years ago. Tabata had shifted over to a quarterly release schedule for the final chapters, and it meant that there were months in between updates. But at the same time, the updated schedule meant that Tabata was able to release multiple chapters at the same time that were much bigger than usual. Given that the creator has been healthy enough to craft new art like this afterwards, it was the best decision Tabata could have made.

What’s Next for Black Clover ?

Black Clover might be over for now, but the franchise is still continuing on with the return of the TV anime adaptation. Kicking off its run this Fall, Black Clover Season 2 has picked up right from the end of the first season from 2017 with all sorts of big battles seen already. The new season is not even halfway into its run, but has provided fans with some of the biggest action moments of the year overall . And there are still many more to go throughout the rest of the season to come.

Black Clover Season 2 has yet to confirm how many episodes it will be running for , but it’s likely not going to be longer than a single cour considering the pace of how it’s been taking on the manga thus far. This is also the pentultimate arc of the series overall, so it’s really all just the beginning of the end for the anime. But what did you think of Black Clover ‘s ending? How are you liking Season 2? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Witch on the Holy Night Film Gets Manga Adaptation
content:
This year's 49th issue of Kodansha 's Weekly Shōnen Magazine announced on Wednesday that the Witch on the Holy Night ( Mahōtsukai no Yoru ) anime film will receive a manga adaptation by Keigo Maki ( Shikimori's Not Just a Cutie ) in the next issue on November 11.

The company streamed a commercial for the upcoming manga, featuring the film's lead cast members Haruka Tomatsu as Aoko Aozaki and Yūsuke Kobayashi as Soujyuro Sizuki:

The story of the original Witch on the Holy Night visual novel is set in the late 1980s, and centers on protagonist Aoko Aozaki, one of two sister heirs to a long family line of modern mages. Although she is disinterested in magic, she is suddenly declared as the heir of their family's magical art, and reluctantly begins her apprenticeship under Alice Kuonji, a young witch who lives in a lonely manor atop a hill. Aoko balances her duties of learning the arcane, while also serving as her school's student council president. She also makes the acquaintance of Sōjūrō Shizuki (romanized as Soujyuro Sizuki in the English version of the game), a new transfer student who is unfamiliar with much of the modern world, and contends with the plots of her older sister Tōko Aozaki, who feels that her birthright has been denied.

The film will open in Japan on November 20. The original visual novel game's smartphone version will launch on the same day as the film's opening in Japan.

Type-Moon most recently released the game on Steam in December 2023.

Aniplex released the PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch versions of the game in the West in December 2022, on the same day as the game's Japanese release date. The PS4 and Switch versions have sold more than 150,000 copies worldwide.

Mahōtsukai no Yoru was one of the first collaborations between Kinoko Nasu and artist Takashi Takeuchi in the mid-90s, preceding their founding of Type-Moon . Initially a novel, Nasu and Takeuchi only showed the draft to friends and did not officially release it. Type-Moon eventually developed it into a visual novel with graphics by Hirokazu Koyama that shipped in April 2012, with two sequels planned.

The story is noted for being one of the few tangible connections in the loosely connected "Nasuverse," the English-speaking fan term for the shared universe and cosmology in Type-Moon 's works, including Tsukihime, Fate/stay night, and The Garden of Sinners . An older Aoko Aozaki is an early mentor to Tsukihime protagonist Shiki Tohno, while an older Tōko Aozaki is an employer to Garden of Sinners protagonist Shiki Ryōgi. Tsukihime -A piece of blue glass moon-, the remake of Type-Moon 's Tsukihime dōjin visual novel game, launched in Japan for PS4 and Switch in August 2021. The game launched on PS4 and Switch in English in June 2024.

title: 'Mashle' Gets Live-Action Movie Adaptation
content:
Production company Warner Bros. Japan announced a live-action movie adaptation of Hajime Koumoto 's Mashle ( Mashle: Magic and Muscles ) manga on Wednesday, revealing a super teaser visual (pictured above). The live-action movie will premiere in Japanese theaters on March 19, 2027.

Warner Bros. Pictures and Fuji TV are credited as production coordinators, while Credeus—the live-action studio behind the Kingdom and Golden Kanuy film series—is producing the live-action adaptation. TOHO is in charge of the distribution.

Koumoto serialized the action comedy manga in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine from January 2020 to July 2023. Shueisha published the 18th and final volume in October 2023. The manga has a cumulative 12 million copies of its volumes in circulation.

VIZ Media simulpublished the manga in English beginning in October 2020 and released the 18th volume in December 2024. Shueisha's Manga Plus platform also simulpublished the manga in English.

A 12-episode television anime adaptation produced by A-1 Pictures aired in Spring 2023, followed by a second season in Winter 2024. A third season is currently in production for a January 2027 premiere.

title: Otaku Vampire's Love Bite Anime Adaptation Announced
content:
Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite manga by Julietta Suzuki ( Kamisama Kiss ) is getting an anime adaptation. A teaser visual and a special trailer were released. The studio, staff, and cast have yet to be announced.

The manga has been serialized in Hakusensha’s shojo manga magazine Hana to Yume since November 2022. It currently has ten volumes in circulation, with the 11th volume set to release this month.

Viz Media is publishing the title in English with nine volumes available. They describe the plot as: Hina’s so busy collecting Mao merch that she almost doesn’t feel bad about missing out on the Vampire Cross cafes. If only she had a human friend who could eat all the themed food for her! But connecting with humans isn’t easy until Hina literally bumps into her neighbor Kyuta, a prickly boy who looks just like Mao. Having her best friend live next door will be so convenient! Now if she can just convince him to actually be her friend… Source: Official website , X (formerly Twitter) © Julietta Suzuki, Hakusensha / “Oshi ni Amagami” Production Committee

title: Crunchyroll’s Hottest New Protagonist Is a Perfect Example of How Modern Anime Heroes Should Be Written
content:
The Fall 2026 season’s darkest and spookiest anime airing on Crunchyroll has the perfect modern protagonist that most new anime are embracing. Older anime, especially shonen series, have always followed a particular format when it comes to their protagonists. The quintessential examples include Goku, Luffy, and Naruto, with their free-spirited, loud, and rowdy personalities, doing whatever they want and following their hearts. Most of these protagonists embark on journeys toward something greater, which eventually ties into saving the world. While this theme isn’t bad, it has become repetitive and no longer fits modern storytelling, where realism is increasingly important.

This is why many recent anime, particularly those embracing darker themes, have introduced more realistic protagonists. Several new shonen anime have followed this approach, including major hits like Jujutsu Kaisen and Gachiakuta . Now, the new dark seinen anime series, The Vermilion Mask , is following the same trend with its protagonist, presenting a new kind of responsibility that comes with power. It portrays a realistic and determined journey rooted in trauma and hardship, with a protagonist who rises above these struggles to help those in need, establishing a new standard for what a hero can be.

Crunchyroll’s Darkest Fall 2026 Anime Has the Perfect Modern Shonen Protagonist

The Vermilion Mask establishes itself as Fall 2026’s darkest anime , and much of that comes from its protagonist enduring one of the most traumatic events imaginable. Peru, an apprentice to a renowned mask maker, experiences a horrific tragedy after wearing a forbidden mask, which results in him killing his master and all the other apprentices. Swearing never to repeat this mistake, Peru embarks on a journey to destroy the masks his master created across the world. However, this is more than just an adventure; it is a journey of self-discovery in which the protagonist understands his role and finds his purpose. Peru’s determination is unlike anything else, as even after losing an arm in the second episode, he continues his journey without hesitation.

This makes his journey even more tragic, but his refusal to abandon his sworn mission highlights an unwavering resolve that viewers can draw inspiration from. These traumatic events are more than enough to push anyone toward the wrong path, yet Peru continues to be a hero through his actions. He has undertaken this journey alone because he doesn’t want anyone else to experience the same tragedy, a resolve further reinforced in the latest episode. After witnessing the events at the museum and seeing a girl in need, Peru emotionally understands the toll she is experiencing, something he can relate to because of his own trauma. He then openly expresses his determination to help her through the situation.

This is a resolve shared by another modern shonen protagonist, Yuji Itadori. He understands his role in the grand scheme of things while still wanting to save every person he encounters along the way. This is what makes Jujutsu Kaisen one of the most modern shonen anime series , almost making it feel like a seinen series at times. Crunchyroll’s new dark anime of Fall 2026, The Vermilion Mask , arguably follows a similar approach with its protagonist, establishing a standard for how modern anime protagonists should be written to resonate with fans.

Now, the new dark seinen anime series, The Vermilion Mask , is following the same trend with its protagonist, presenting a new kind of responsibility that comes with power. It portrays a realistic and determined journey rooted in trauma and hardship, with a protagonist who rises above these struggles to help those in need, establishing a new standard for what a hero can be.
Crunchyroll’s Darkest Fall 2026 Anime Has the Perfect Modern Shonen Protagonist

The Vermilion Mask establishes itself as Fall 2026’s darkest anime , and much of that comes from its protagonist enduring one of the most traumatic events imaginable. Peru, an apprentice to a renowned mask maker, experiences a horrific tragedy after wearing a forbidden mask, which results in him killing his master and all the other apprentices. Swearing never to repeat this mistake, Peru embarks on a journey to destroy the masks his master created across the world. However, this is more than just an adventure; it is a journey of self-discovery in which the protagonist understands his role and finds his purpose. Peru’s determination is unlike anything else, as even after losing an arm in the second episode, he continues his journey without hesitation.

This makes his journey even more tragic, but his refusal to abandon his sworn mission highlights an unwavering resolve that viewers can draw inspiration from. These traumatic events are more than enough to push anyone toward the wrong path, yet Peru continues to be a hero through his actions. He has undertaken this journey alone because he doesn’t want anyone else to experience the same tragedy, a resolve further reinforced in the latest episode. After witnessing the events at the museum and seeing a girl in need, Peru emotionally understands the toll she is experiencing, something he can relate to because of his own trauma. He then openly expresses his determination to help her through the situation.

This is a resolve shared by another modern shonen protagonist, Yuji Itadori. He understands his role in the grand scheme of things while still wanting to save every person he encounters along the way. This is what makes Jujutsu Kaisen one of the most modern shonen anime series , almost making it feel like a seinen series at times. Crunchyroll’s new dark anime of Fall 2026, The Vermilion Mask , arguably follows a similar approach with its protagonist, establishing a standard for how modern anime protagonists should be written to resonate with fans.

title: Otaku Vampire's Love Bite Manga Gets TV Anime
content:
ShoPro Entertainment announced with a teaser promotional video and visual on Wednesday that Julietta Suzuki 's Otaku Vampire's Love Bite ( Oshi ni Amagami ) manga will receive a television anime adaptation.

Viz Media publishes the series in English and describes the story:

Even vampires obsess over their favorite characters! After spending 30 years as a shut-in, the vampire Hina moves to Japan to enjoy otaku activities. There, she meets her neighbor, Kyuta Amanatsu, a boy who looks just like her favorite character! What's more, his blood is something special, irresistible to vampires everywhere. As other vampires show up with their sights set on Kyuta, his relationship with Hina takes an unexpected turn. Is she fangirling…or falling in love?! A 100% otaku vampire meets a handsome, slightly sharp-tongued guy in this bloody romantic comedy!

Suzuki launched the manga in Hakusensha 's Hana to Yume magazine in November 2022. Hakusensha shipped the 10th compiled book volume on July 17 and will ship the 11th volume on November 20. Viz Media shipped the eighth volume on July 7 and will ship the ninth volume on December 1.

The manga is a serialization of a one-shot with the same title that Suzuki published in Hana to Yume in April 2022.

Suzuki ended the Meitantei Kо̄ko wa Yūutsu (Detective Kо̄ko Is Melancholy) manga in June 2022. Suzuki published a one-shot for the manga in Hana to Yume January 2020, before serializing it in the magazine in September 2020.

Suzuki launched the Kamisama Kiss manga in Hana to Yume in 2008, and ended the series in May 2016 with 25 volumes. Viz Media has published the manga in English.

Kamisama Kiss inspired two anime seasons. Funimation streamed both seasons as they aired in Japan, and also released both seasons on home video. The manga also inspired a series of four original anime DVDs (OADs) that shipped with the manga's 22nd through 25th compiled volumes. A "volume 25.5," an official fanbook, shipped in December 2016. The fanbook bundled a DVD with an original anime and a 32-page epilogue manga.

title: Manga 'Oshi ni Amagami' Receives TV Anime Adaptation
content:
Production company Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions announced a television anime adaptation of Julietta Suzuki 's Oshi ni Amagami ( Otaku Vampire's Love Bite ) manga on Wednesday, revealing special visual (pictured) and announcement promo.

Suzuki began serializing the comedy romance manga in Hana to Yume magazine in April 2022. Hakusensha published the tenth volume on July 17, with the 11th volume scheduled to be released on November 20.

VIZ Media licensed the manga in English in February 2024. The eighth volume went on sale on July 7, with the ninth scheduled for a December 1 release.

Oshi ni Amagami was nominated for the 14th An An Manga Award in 2023.

Synopsis Hina Arukado is a modern vampire who drinks blood from bags instead of humans. But she's also a complete shut-in who hasn't left the house in 30 years. In an effort to reach her, Hina's worried dad does something that changes her life—he gives her the complete box set of the Vampire Cross anime series! Hina is instantly obsessed with everything about the show, especially the character Mao. But it's hard to fan as hard as she wants from her bedroom in Romania, so now Hina is out of the house and off to Japan to live her otaku dream!

Japan is otaku heaven for Hina, and she's so busy collecting as much merch as her new apartment can hold that she almost doesn't feel bad about missing out on the special menus at Vampire Cross cafes. If only she had a human friend who could eat all the themed food for her! But connecting with humans isn't easy until Hina literally bumps into her neighbor Kyuta, a prickly boy who looks just like Mao. Having her best friend live next door will be so convenient! If she can just convince him to actually be friends… (Source: VIZ Media)
